title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for diabetes and kidney disease.

HPI: The patient presents today for a routine follow-up of type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease stage 4. The patient reports feeling stable and has been adhering to their current management plan. They report that their blood glucose levels are stable and they have not experienced any new symptoms related to their kidney function. The patient notes that their diabetes is currently diet controlled.

Medication List: No medications listed.

Exam: The patient is alert and oriented. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical exam shows no acute distress. Skin is intact and no edema is noted in the lower extremities.

Assessment: 1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Currently stable and managed through diet and exercise. 2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: The patient's renal decline is noted to be unrelated to diabetes.

Plan: Continue current lifestyle modifications and dietary restrictions. The patient will return in three months for a follow-up laboratory evaluation and clinical review.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes, so the presumed link does not apply: code diabetes without complications and CKD separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.

distractors.why: The 'with' presumption is overridden when the provider documents another cause or no link.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
